title: A Thousand Passengers, One Bridge
tagline: Three thousand people aboard, a storm system closing in on the planned route, and a bridge crew waiting on your call.

wake_up.text: The overnight weather report is on your desk before you've even had coffee — a storm system has shifted, and it's now closer to tomorrow's planned route than anyone expected.

choices.text: Study the full weather system yourself before the morning briefing
Trust your navigator's summary and move on

bridge_briefing.text: Morning bridge briefing: the storm system, today's port call, and three thousand passengers who all have their own itinerary riding on your decisions.

choices.text: Begin the morning watch

random_moment.text: The morning watch on the bridge has its own quiet rhythm — a little different every day.

choices.text: The bridge crew shares a genuinely good laugh over coffee
A radar display glitches briefly before resetting itself
The seas are unusually calm this morning

port_authority_call.text: Port authority calls about tonight's scheduled arrival — they want confirmation given the storm system's shifting track.

choices.text: Commit to the original schedule, weather permitting
Flag a possible delay now, before it becomes urgent

morning_rounds.text: A walk through the ship — engine room, guest services, the kitchens — the part of the job that reminds you how many people's day depends on this ship running smoothly.

choices.text: Return to the bridge

storm_decision.text: The storm system has intensified faster than forecast. Staying on course cuts hours off the trip but sails closer to rough water than you'd like; diverting protects the ship but means disappointing three thousand people's port day, and the decision has to go out to the whole ship in the next few minutes.

choices.text: Divert course immediately and announce it
Hold course and monitor the system closely before deciding
Get the ship's meteorologist on the bridge before deciding anything
Choose a partial reroute that splits the difference

storm_outcome_divert.text: The ship turns well clear of the worst of it. Passengers grumble about the missed port call, but the crossing stays smooth the whole way through — exactly the kind of decision nobody thanks you for making correctly.

choices.text: Address the passengers directly

storm_outcome_hold.text: Holding course saves the port call, and the ship rides out rougher water than anyone would have liked — nothing broke, but it was closer than the forecast promised, and the bridge crew knows it.

choices.text: Continue toward port

storm_outcome_consult.text: The meteorologist's updated read shows a safe corridor nobody else had spotted yet — a genuinely good, ten-minutes-costlier decision that gets you both the port call and the safety margin.

choices.text: Adjust course along the safe corridor

storm_outcome_partial.text: The partial reroute adds two hours but keeps the ship well clear of the worst cells. Not the cleanest call in hindsight, but a reasonable one made with the information available at the time.

choices.text: Continue on the adjusted route

afternoon_watch.text: Guest services radios the bridge: a passenger has collapsed near the pool deck, and the ship's small medical team wants your call on whether to divert for a medical evacuation.

choices.text: Divert toward the nearest port for medical evacuation
Trust the ship's medical team to stabilize the passenger

vip_dinner.text: Captain's dinner tonight, a tradition passengers look forward to, on a day that's given you very little room to look forward to anything.

choices.text: Attend and be genuinely present for it
Make a brief appearance and get back to the bridge

evening_watch.text: Evening watch, the ship settling into its night rhythm. Tomorrow's port arrival still depends on how the night unfolds.

choices.text: Do a personal final check of tomorrow's approach plan
Hand the watch to your officer of the deck and rest

end_shift.text: The ship moves on through the dark, three thousand people asleep or dancing somewhere below, all of it resting on a bridge that never actually stops.

choices.text: Retire to your quarters

triumphant.title: The Captain They'll Remember
triumphant.blurb: Every call today was the right one, made calmly, under real pressure. This is the crossing passengers talk about for years.

steady_hand.title: Safe Passage
steady_hand.blurb: No headlines, no incidents — just careful, competent command, mile after mile.

ordinary_day.title: Routine Crossing
ordinary_day.blurb: A normal day at sea, weather handled, passengers content. Tomorrow's port call is already on the schedule.

burned_out.title: Running on Empty
burned_out.blurb: You made it through the watch, but you're not sure how. This pace, decision after decision, has a real cost.

written_up.title: Incident Report Filed
written_up.blurb: Something about today's calls is heading into a formal review with the line. Everyone's safe. The company still wants answers.
